summary: Ute Wallenböck is a sinologist and tibetologist who earned degrees at the University of Vienna and Sigmund Freud University. She held posts at Vienna, Palacký University Olomouc, Masaryk University (2019–2024), and the University of Bonn (2024).

Uto von Melzer was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Graz (1919–1923), having studied under Johann Kirste, Rudolf Meringer, and Hans Reichelt.

Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (1965–1972). He served as Universitätsdozent at Vienna in 1969 and completed a research stay at the University of Madras from 1972 to 1974.

V. I. Subramoniam was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Annamalai University and Indiana University Bloomington. He served at the University of Kerala, was the first Vice-Chancellor of Tamil University, and co-founded and served Dravidian University.
V. Kameswari is an Indologist associated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where she is attested as an Editorial Committee member in 2001 and as a supervisor/guide in 2026.
V. M. Subramanya Sharma is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as an Assistant Professor at Osmania University from 2011 to 2022 and at the University of Delhi in 2022.

Vinayaka P. Bhatta is an Indologist and linguist associated with the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, serving as head of the Sanskrit Dictionary Project (attested 2011) and later as Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).

V. R. Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Attested in 2026, he was a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

V. Raghavan was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He taught at Madras (1934–1968), founded the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and held posts at the Madras Music Academy.

V. W. Paranjpe was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi. He served as Superintendent of the Publication Department at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1927) and later became Professor Emeritus at Deccan College.
Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Reading in 2017 and held a post there in 2018.

Vairamuthu Kanagaraj is an Indology scholar who earned an MA at SASTRA and is pursuing a PhD at IIT Hyderabad. He served at the National Institute of Indian Medical Heritage, Jayadev Memorial Rashtrotthana Hospital, and IIT Hyderabad.

Valaiyattur Venkayya was an epigraphist and scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He served as Acting Government Epigraphist for Madras and the Archaeological Survey of India.

Valdo H. Viglielmo was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy. Educated at Harvard, the University of Tokyo, and Gakushuin, he taught at Meiji Gakuin, Harvard, and Princeton before serving as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1965–2002).

Valentin Parisot was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the École Normale Supérieure. He served as Professor of Foreign Literature at the University of Rennes (1842–1847), Grenoble Alpes University (1847–1853), and the University of Douai (1854).

Valentin Trapp was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich. He also studied at Visva-Bharati and Banaras Hindu University under Hanns Oertel, Lucian Scherman, Walther Wüst, Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, Kshitimohan Sen, and Gyula Germanus.

Valentina Stache-Rosen was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt (1944–1954) and also studied at SOAS University of London and Deccan College.

Valentine Ball was an Indology scholar educated at Trinity College Dublin. He worked with the Geological Survey of India (1864–1881), taught as Professor of Geology and Mineralogy at Trinity (1881–1883), and directed the National Museum of Ireland (1883–1895).
Valentino Papesso was an Indologist who studied at the University of Bologna from approximately 1907 to 1911 and later served there as Docent of Sanskrit from around 1925 to 1944.
Valeria Gazizova is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed her master's thesis at the University of Oslo under Hanna Havnevik and MA supervisor Per Kværne.
